doc: PROFILE.md §6.1: '`filters.georeference` and `filters.straighten`. Two new filters.' A new filter is registered when the application's own driver listing names it, and `pdal --drivers` is the listing §6.1 uses for this step's other two new stages; apps/index.rst gives the invocation as its own example, '`$ pdal --drivers`'. `new-stage-options` grades the option table through a different switch, `pdal --options <stage>`, so the two groups observe different things and can fail independently. Registration is the gradeable half of `filters.straighten`: stages/filters.straighten.rst makes `polyline` -- a definition 'of a 3D linestring with measurment (LINESTRING ZM in wkt) along which the cloud will be straighten' -- mandatory, 'This is mandatory', and the page's own two examples elide the geometry, so no runnable value for it is stated anywhere in this corpus. `--drivers` prints a two-column reST table with the driver name at column 0, so the case matches the name at the start of a line and reads nothing else: the description column, the row's position in the table and the number of rows are not stated by any shipped page and are not graded. Note the exit status is 0 at BOTH anchors -- what discriminates is that the row is absent from the 2.5.0 table and present at 2.6.0, not the status.
